page: Amazon Web Services c8g.2xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized virtual server instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped directly to 8 physical cores based on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptographic operations. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB of RAM allocated per physical core.

Hardware configurations exclude integrated local disk storage and GPU accelerators, relying entirely on networked storage volumes via the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations place the instance predominantly within average performance bands, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 9878.0 and a multi-core stress-ng CPU result of 13647.2. Data processing benchmarks demonstrate strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.22 GB/sec, while static web serving achieves 19.82 GB/sec and in-memory Redis SET operations deliver 18.14 million operations per second.

Performance tradeoffs become evident in cryptographic and specialized machine learning workloads. The instance registers weaker results in the PassMark CPU encryption benchmark at 1509.87 and delivers poor performance in 7B LLM prompt processing at 15.58 tokens per second. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the 1:2 memory ratio and dedicated core model maximize CPU compute allocation per gigabyte of RAM without hyperthreading overhead.

The c8g.2xlarge server is suited for CPU-bound tasks such as software compilation, batch processing pipelines, web application serving, and distributed microservices that do not require local NVMe caching, hardware graphics accelerators, or large memory footprints.
description: Amazon Web Services c8g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture and managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 8 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz without hyperthreading, coupled with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance includes 36 MB of shared L3 cache and a 4 Gbps baseline network interface, while omitting local instance storage and dedicated GPU hardware. Synthetic testing reflects steady multi-core execution, highlighted by 13647.2 in stress-ng multi-core and 14.22 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression, alongside 18.14 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, performance lags in cryptographic testing and 7B LLM prompt processing. The c8g.2xlarge provides cost-efficient CPU resource allocation for microservices, Clang build environments, CI/CD runners, and general compute-oriented Linux workloads.
